clue.text: No one's at home here

parts.note: a sports venue where neither team is playing on its own home pitch

explanation.surface: An empty house, with nobody in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a deserted building; the real sense is a match venue that belongs to neither side.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixture on neutral turf gives no side home advantage, so no team is 'at home' there.

clue.text: Self-indulgent action to gripe about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the words to gripe are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complaining just to indulge themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal, rearranging TOGRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanity venture undertaken chiefly to flatter oneself is the standard sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Put one's foot down back in Tudor times

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Tudor times

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asserting authority in the sixteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters DORT within 'Tudor times' and 'back' turns them round; the draft lacked the 'in' indicator, now added.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of tread: to have placed a foot on the ground is literally to have put it down.

clue.text: Those beastly overheads

parts.note: the branched horns worn above the head by deer and similar beasts

explanation.surface: A grumble about horrible business running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' means belonging to beasts, and 'overheads' means things over the head, not costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer carry these bony branched growths on top of their heads, literally over them.

clue.text: Cargo transported up street in small fast vehicles

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters of Cargo are moved into a new arrangement
up in a down clue says the abbreviation is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Goods carried along a road by quick little vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges CARGO to GOCAR; 'up' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small, low motor vehicles raced around tracks, quick for their size.

clue.text: Look round over leg in play

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the next

parts.note: a round shape resembles the letter O

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters of leg are being moved about freely

explanation.surface: A cricket or theatre scene: glancing round at a leg in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges LEG to GLE, set beneath O since 'over' works positionally in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone with obvious interest is a particular kind of looking.

clue.text: Point is needed to beat old club

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
to lick someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Advice that a sharp edge is needed to defeat a long-established sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old golf iron with a lofted face, roughly today's nine iron.

clue.text: Not fit, thought to be rash

parts.note: someone not fit is unwell, ill
considered means thought, as in 'it was considered unlikely'

explanation.surface: A sick person reckoned to have a skin eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' reads as a skin complaint beside 'Not fit', but it means hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision made without proper reflection is hasty and reckless, which is what rash means.

clue.text: Shoe with a tongue, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe
a tongue is a language, such as English

explanation.surface: A shoe has a tongue, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoe with a tongue' pictures footwear, but the tongue is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a refined, educated accent and form of the language, a way of talking.

clue.text: Take care to not be introspective

definitions.meaning: to direct one's gaze outward rather than looking inward

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful and not to brood on oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means beware, and also literally gazing outward, the opposite of introspection.

clue.text: Title fight in booth

parts.note: to call someone something is to give them a title or name
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A championship belt bout held in a small booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title fight' looks like a boxing contest; it splits into name and fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone kiosk is a public booth from which calls are made.

clue.text: Short cut that's about right

indicators.note: about says the word cut goes round the next piece

explanation.surface: A trimmed haircut that is roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque, rudely brief reply is described as short.

clue.text: Listened and learned

definitions.meaning: took in sound, perceived by ear
found out, as in 'I gather that...'

explanation.surface: A pupil who paid attention and took it in.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the hearing verb means both perceived by ear and been told about.

clue.text: Today's most popular writer?

parts.note: the writer is a pen, not an author: the ballpoint everyone uses

explanation.surface: A question about the current best-selling author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests a novelist; it is the writing instrument. Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballpoint pen is the most widely used writing implement in the modern era.

clue.text: Form of tribunal?

definitions.meaning: a form is a long backless seat
a body of judges or magistrates sitting together

explanation.surface: A question about the constitution of a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like 'type', but it is an old word for a long seat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long seat, and collectively the judges or magistrates hearing a case.

clue.text: Extra payment on getting into public transport

indicators.note: getting into says the word on is placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Extra pay for a commute aboard buses or trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid over and above normal wages is an additional reward payment.

clue.text: Relatives getting directions — sighs of relief!

parts.note: N and E are the compass directions north and east
phew is an exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Family members relieved to be given the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's sons are kin, close family relations.

clue.text: Horrified by current events?

definitions.meaning: jolted by electric current, given an electric jolt

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current events' reads as the news, but current is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means appalled, and also having received an electric jolt.

clue.text: Add fifty-one to one-and-fifty. Hundred? It is not right!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I and fifty is L
fifty is the Roman numeral L and one is I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A sum done wrong: someone protests the arithmetic is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures are Roman numerals: IL then LI, followed by C and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by law or rules is improper, contrary to what is permitted.

clue.text: In France the one indisputable freedom

parts.note: le is French for the
one is the Roman numeral I
sure means certain, beyond dispute

explanation.surface: A patriotic claim about France's one undeniable liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time is time released from work, freedom to do as one pleases.

clue.text: Soldiers welcome sailors inside foreign restaurant

indicators.note: inside says the welcome and the sailors go within the soldiers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
ave is a Latin greeting, hail
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Troops greeting naval men inside a restaurant abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Greek eating house, a restaurant of foreign origin.

clue.text: Warn one that's amusing

explanation.surface: A caution about a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means admonish; informally a highly amusing person is called a caution.

clue.text: Summons? Nothing to us, being hardened

parts.note: a call is a summons
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A legal writ that means nothing to people grown indifferent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insensitive to suffering is emotionally toughened, unfeeling.

clue.text: Competitors will be on edge in this arena

definitions.text: Competitors will be on edge in this arena

parts.words: Competitors will be on edge in this arena
parts.note: skaters balance on the edges of their blades in a frozen venue

explanation.surface: Tense athletes in a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like nervousness; it means on skate edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaters compete on the blade edges of their skates in this frozen arena.

clue.text: Farewell issue

definitions.meaning: to issue is to come out, go out

explanation.surface: A final edition of a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a magazine number; it means going out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a leave-taking, and also to go out or emerge.

clue.text: A lump in one's throat

parts.note: the fleshy flap hanging at the back of the mouth, literally in the throat

explanation.surface: The choked feeling of strong emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means being moved; read literally it is the small fleshy lobe at the back of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy pendant hanging from the soft palate is an actual lump in the throat.

clue.text: Work as a bank clerk and present an account

definitions.meaning: a bank cashier counts money, which the old verb means

explanation.surface: A bank employee reporting on a customer's account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account' suggests a bank account; it means a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means count money as a cashier does, and also recount or narrate.

clue.text: Having no work to do, some take unpaid leave

indicators.note: some says only part of the words unpaid leave is used

explanation.surface: Without a job, some people go on unpaid leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inactive and unemployed means lacking any occupation.

clue.text: Horse's blaze of celebrity

definitions.meaning: a white patch on a horse's forehead

explanation.surface: A racehorse's fiery fame.
explanation.walkthrough: A blaze is a white mark on a horse's face, here a small one on the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the white forehead mark on a horse and also a famous performer.

clue.text: Old European currency used on road repairing somewhere in S America

parts.note: the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

indicators.note: repairing suggests the letters of road are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Old euro funds spent on mending a road in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a republic on the Pacific coast of the continent, straddling the equator.

clue.text: Gets messing about in boats

indicators.note: messing about suggests the letters of in boats are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys messing about in boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'messing about in boats' from The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire or procure something is to get it.

clue.text: Everybody's out in the CO's three-wheeler

parts.note: a CO, commanding officer, may be a general; the possessive gives the S
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Everyone is out riding in the commanding officer's tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means on strike, not absent.
explanation.definitionFit: When workers across all industries stop work together, everyone is out on strike.
